list.name: namespace
list.label: Namespace
list.description: Fed from kube-state-metrics, never from process_start_time_seconds: box is minReplicaCount 0, so a process-lifecycle metric leaves this variable — and every panel, including the backlog and KEDA rows that survive the sleeping pod — empty in the connector's normal state.

list.name: pod
list.label: Pod
list.description: allValue is .+ and not .*: every series is scraped twice in dev (PodMonitor plus the kubernetes-services catch-all) and only the PodMonitor copy carries a pod label. In PromQL .* also matches the absent label, which doubles every additive aggregation while leaving percentiles and _sum/_count ratios correct — so the board would be internally inconsistent with no obviously broken panel.

panels.title: Totals in Window
panels.description: Counters totalled over the selected range, not averaged as a rate. Box scales to zero: a scan that finishes inside one scrape interval moves the counter 0 to N entirely between scrapes, and rate() over it is exactly 0 — not a small number. Read this row first, then the backlog row to tell idle from stuck.

panels.title: Files Discovered (total)
panels.description: File entries seen in folder listings, before any filtering. The funnel's denominator.

panels.title: Items Sent (total)
panels.description: Files the scanner handed to the item sender. The only success path out of the scan.

panels.title: Item Loss (total)

targets.expr: (sum(max_over_time(box_scanner_files_discovered_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) - (sum(max_over_time(box_scanner_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__range])) or vector(0))

panels.description: Discovered minus every terminal outcome. Should be zero: a non-zero value means an exit path in processFolder is uninstrumented, not that files were lost.

panels.title: Users Enumerated (total)
panels.description: Enterprise users listed at the start of a full scan. In Box the unit of fan-out is the user, so this is the real denominator of a scan.

panels.title: Folders Forked (total)
panels.description: Subfolders published to NATS as box.folder. Every subfolder becomes its own message, so this is the number of traversal units the scan created — and it is NOT proportional to files: a deep tree of empty folders still produces messages here.

panels.title: Content Fetches (total)
panels.description: ContentFetchRequest deliveries resolved by the content pods, success and failure together.

panels.title: Users — Fan-out Funnel
panels.description: Box's own failure mode, with no equivalent in a per-directory connector: the unit of fan-out is the user, so each skip costs one person's entire content while the rest of the scan still reports success. None of it shows up in the file funnel below — those files were never discovered.

panels.title: Users Enumerated
panels.description: GET /users, paged. The denominator.

panels.title: Users Forked

targets.expr: (sum(max_over_time(box_scanner_users_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) - (sum(max_over_time(box_scanner_users_skipped_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__range])) or vector(0))

panels.description: Enumerated minus skipped: the users a box.fork was actually published for.

panels.title: Users Skipped
panels.description: Users whose content was not scanned at all, any reason. Counted once per user — the per-folder TOS path is deliberately excluded, since one TOS-blocked person has thousands of folders and would read as thousands of skipped users.

panels.title: Skip Rate

targets.expr: 100 * ((sum(max_over_time(box_scanner_users_skipped_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min((sum(max_over_time(box_scanner_users_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__range])) or vector(0)), 1))

panels.description: Share of the enterprise whose content this scan did not cover.

panels.title: Users Skipped by Reason (total in window)
panels.description: All six reasons are exported at 0 even when nobody is skipped (InitUserSkipReasons), so an empty stack means the scan ran clean rather than that the series is missing. Only traverse_failed is a connector failure; permission_denied is broken config, and the other four are expected absence.

panels.title: User Fan-out over time (rate, 5m)
panels.description: Only legible under sustained load. With a burst that finishes inside a scrape interval both lines read 0 — use the stats above for that case.

panels.title: Scanner — box-connector-be-go
panels.description: There are deliberately no ACL panels here: the scanner's collaboration fetch is commented out in folder_work.go to save API tokens, so ACLs come only from the augmenter. A scanner ACL panel would be flat by design, which on a board is indistinguishable from a broken one.

panels.title: Pods Up
panels.description: Zero is the normal state, not an outage: minReplicaCount is 0 and the cooldown is 900s.

panels.title: Items Failed (5m)
panels.description: Total items the scanner discovered but could not deliver: build_failed and upsert_failed added together. This is the headline loss count. For WHICH of the two it was, see 'Scanner Items by Outcome' — build_failed is bad data, upsert_failed is the sender or NATS.

panels.title: Folder p95
panels.description: One BoxFolderWork message: a single folder listing plus its publishes and upserts. This is the connector's real unit of work, and the one that makes cost predictable.

panels.title: Folder Work In-Flight
panels.description: Folder handlers running right now across the selected pods. BoxFork and BoxFolderWork both count — both process a folder.

panels.title: User Slots Held
panels.description: Cross-pod per-user admission slots held. Read against the deferral counter in the API row: slots at the cap with deferrals rising means BOX_USER_MAX_CONCURRENCY is what binds.

panels.title: Scanner Throughput (rate, 5m)
panels.description: Three near-parallel lines; the question is the gap between them. The pipeline board graphs that difference explicitly, which is the only way funnel loss is actually visible.

panels.title: Scanner Items by Outcome (rate, 5m)
panels.description: skipped_inactive is the scanner's half of Files Gone: the file was already in Box's trash when we listed its parent. A different moment from the incremental path's deleted outcome — see the Files Gone row, and do not add them.

panels.title: Folder Duration — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: One BoxFolderWork message: one folder listing plus the publishes and upserts it produces. This is the connector's real unit of work — multiply its mean by a folder count to estimate a larger tenant.

panels.title: Folders by Outcome (rate, 5m)
panels.description: Every subfolder is forked as its own message. skipped_collab is the owner filter: a folder owned by another user, left for that user's own fork so it is enumerated exactly once.

panels.title: Saturation — in-flight, slots, deferrals
panels.description: Where the scanner throttles itself. Box rate-limits per impersonated user, so the connector holds a fixed number of slots per user shared across every pod; work that finds no free slot is deferred and redelivered later. Flat at zero with the pods asleep is the normal state; flat WITH load would mean only one of the two folder entry points got instrumented.

panels.title: Scan Durations — three different units
panels.description: Three genuinely different measurements, plotted together for scale only — they are not comparable. fan-out is authenticate plus paged GET /users plus publishing one box.fork per user, and EXCLUDES the traversal. incremental is a whole run including its inline augment. root_folder is one BoxFork: a user's root level only, not their tree. 'How long did the scan take end to end' is not answerable from the connector at all — a scan is a fan-out of messages with no owner.

panels.title: Scanner — Backlog & Autoscaling
panels.description: These series live on the broker and on kube-state-metrics, so they survive scale-to-zero and answer 'how far behind is it?' in the state the connector spends most of its time in.

panels.title: NATS — Redelivered
panels.description: A connector that fails and retries in a loop shows up here and nowhere else.

panels.title: Max Replicas
panels.description: The KEDA ceiling as the HPA reports it. The value comes from the chart (autoscaling.maxReplicas) and differs per environment, so read it off the panel rather than assuming one. Desired-equals-max is not by itself a sign of trouble — read it together with the backlog: at a low ceiling it is reached routinely.

panels.title: NATS — Backlog Slope (2m)
panels.description: The trend-based trigger's own signal: messages per second the backlog is growing by.

panels.title: NATS — Scanner Consumer Backlog
panels.description: Stream JE_BOX, durable box-scanner-v1. Sustained ack_pending with items_sent at zero is the signature of a stuck connector.

panels.title: KEDA — Replicas: current vs desired vs max
panels.description: cooldownPeriod 900s and scaleDown stabilizationWindowSeconds 600s. 'It scaled ten minutes ago and is still the same' is config, not a bug.

panels.title: KEDA — ack-capacity signal vs threshold
panels.description: replicas = ceil(ack_pending / threshold), with the threshold set by the ScaledObject. The red line is that threshold as configured in this environment; crossing it is what asks for another pod.

panels.title: KEDA — trend-based signal vs threshold
panels.description: Threshold 0.5, activation 0.1. Positive slope means the backlog is growing.

panels.title: KEDA — pending-wakeup signal vs threshold
panels.description: The trigger that wakes the pod from zero: its activation threshold is 0, so a single pending message is enough. The red line is the scale threshold as configured here. The fourth trigger, pipeline-full, is NOT rendered in dev — pipelineFull.capacity is empty in the chart and the environment does not override it — so it is deliberately absent rather than drawn as a flat panel.

panels.title: Box API — Saturation
panels.description: In an API connector the scarce resource is Box's rate limit: roughly 16.67 req/s for the whole app, shared across every pod. None of these series carries a tenant label — the HTTP client has no datasource_id in scope — so this row cannot be filtered by datasource. Attribution lives in the scanner funnel instead.

panels.title: API Calls (5m)
panels.description: HTTP attempts, not logical calls: doJSON retries up to BOX_MAX_RETRIES, so one GetFile can be four requests. Calls rising faster than items means we are retrying.

panels.title: Limiter Wait p95
panels.description: The LEADING saturation signal: time spent waiting on our own token bucket before a request goes out. Lowering BOX_RATE_LIMIT_PER_SEC must move this first — if it does not, the signal is not wired.

panels.title: 429s (5m)
panels.description: The LAGGING half: Box has already refused us. Known blind spot — only doJSON counts here, so a 429 on the content download path (GetFileContent, probeGet) is invisible on this series today.

panels.title: Slot Deferrals (5m)
panels.description: Fork/folder messages NAKed with a 5s delay because the impersonated user was already at BOX_USER_MAX_CONCURRENCY across all pods.

panels.title: API Calls by Endpoint (rate, 5m)
panels.description: Ten fixed templates, passed in by each client method rather than parsed off the URL. folder_items should dominate during a scan. The four /events values are kept apart on purpose: the cursor read is one or two pages, the admin-log backfill runs up to 200 pages per refresh, and the per-user pull runs up to 50 pages FOR EVERY USER — collapsing them would hide the one that can run away.

panels.title: API Calls by Status (rate, 5m)
panels.description: transport_error is a request that never got a response — connection reset, timeout, DNS. Deliberately distinct from any HTTP code, so 'Box refused us' and 'we never reached Box' are not the same bucket.

panels.title: Saturation — leading vs lagging
panels.description: The pair that makes tuning legible. The limiter p95 must rise BEFORE the 429s do. Note the limiter is per pod while Box's ceiling is per app, so a single pod can look idle while Box throttles the whole deployment — the sum across pods is the number to compare against the ceiling.

panels.title: API Call Duration p95 by Endpoint
panels.description: Round-trip only, deliberately excluding the limiter wait below it, so 'is Box slow' and 'are we throttling ourselves' stay separable. For file_content this is time-to-first-byte, NOT the download — that leg is box_content_transfer_duration_seconds, and reading it as the download is wrong by orders of magnitude.

panels.title: Rate Limiter Wait — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: Sub-second is the interesting range; the ladder starts at 1ms.

panels.title: Augmenter — box-connector-be-go
panels.description: The augment path re-fetches each previously discovered file from Box to attach collaborations and an approximated last-access date. It is the only source of ACLs in the connector today.

panels.title: Augmenter Items by Outcome (rate, 5m)
panels.description: sent_without_acl is degraded success, not failure: when ListFileCollaborations fails the item is emitted anyway (stale metadata beats no metadata). Counting it as plain success is what made the old board overstate data quality. outcome=missing is also counted by items_skipped_not_found_total for the same event — never sum the two.

panels.title: last_access Coverage
panels.description: hit / (hit + miss) answers how much of the last_access we emit is real rather than unknown. The events-loaded rate underneath is the denominator behind it: a hit rate falling while events stop loading is a stale store, not a data problem.

panels.title: Augment Batch Duration — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: Carries no datasource_id on purpose: the observation is deferred at the top of AugmentScan and the id is only recovered further in, per access-id group. So this is the one augmenter panel the pipeline board cannot break down by datasource — it still filters by namespace and pod, which come from the scrape, not from the instrument.

panels.title: Content — box-connector-be-go-content
panels.description: CONNECTOR_MODE=content streams Box file bytes into content-service. These series are labeled by datasource_access_id, not datasource_id: the URN content is handed carries only access, file_id and user_id, so the datasource_id genuinely does not exist in this mode.

panels.title: Upload Throughput
panels.description: Bytes content-service confirmed in its UploadResponse — what the far side acknowledged, not what Box declared.

panels.title: NATS — Fetch Backlog
panels.description: Bulk and interactive durables together.

panels.title: Content Fetches by error_code (rate, 5m)
panels.description: NONE is the success case. The NAK_* codes are infra failures before or after a wire reply, where no FetchErrorCode applies — counting them is what makes fetch_total equal the number of deliveries the handler processed, not just the ones that produced a terminal reply. Timeout and too-large are error_code values here rather than their own counters, so an alert can target any code without a new series.

panels.title: Transfer p95 by size_bucket

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, size_bucket) (rate(box_content_transfer_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod", success="true"}[5m])))

panels.description: Answers 'is the latency per file or per byte?'. Because the size is known before the transfer starts (Content-Length), it works on the failure path too — flip success to false. The unknown bucket is Box omitting Content-Length, not a zero-byte file, which is why it is not grouped with the small ones.

panels.title: NATS — Content Consumer Backlog
panels.description: Two durables share the CONTENT_FETCH stream: content-fetch-box for the bulk lane and content-fetch-box-interactive for See-Content. Split by consumer_name so an interactive-only backlog is visible instead of averaged away.

panels.title: KEDA — Content Replicas: current vs desired vs max
KEDA — Content Trigger Signals
panels.description: Three of the content ScaledObject's four effective triggers, all against the bulk durable. pipeline-full is not rendered in dev.

panels.title: KEDA — interactive-wakeup signal vs threshold
panels.description: The fourth trigger, and the one the scanner does not have: it watches the See-Content durable so an interactive-only backlog still wakes the pod. Without it scale-to-zero would strand every See-Content request into a 504.

panels.title: Data Quality — Files Gone
panels.description: Box answers 'how many files are no longer there?' at THREE stages, and they are deliberately not summable: each is a different moment in the pipeline and is diagnosed differently. The incremental one is the cleanest signal in the whole set — it comes from an explicit ITEM_TRASH/DELETE event from Box, not from a NOT_FOUND inferred after the fact.

panels.title: Gone — seen in trash by the scan
panels.description: Already in Box's trash at the moment we listed its parent folder.

panels.title: Gone — deleted per the event stream
panels.description: An ITEM_TRASH or DELETE event resolved by an incremental run.

panels.title: Gone — 404 on augment re-fetch
panels.description: Discovered by an earlier scan, and Box answered 404 when the augmenter went back for it.

panels.title: Files Gone by stage (rate, 5m)
panels.description: Three series, never one number. The augment series is 1:1 with box_augmenter_items_skipped_not_found_total — the same event increments both, and that second counter exists only so alerts can suppress this expected signal separately. Graphing both would be the same thing counted twice.

panels.title: Files Gone % (augment)

targets.expr: 100 * ((sum(max_over_time(box_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod", outcome="missing"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min((sum(max_over_time(box_augmenter_items_processed_total{namespace="$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__range])) or vector(0)), 1))

panels.description: Share of everything the augmenter touched that Box no longer had.
